issues.description: Element: SealSaloon.stock (the saloon's Stock field). Contradiction: The UML and earlier textual description in the problem statement (UML block and the paragraph describing required attributes) state that SealSaloon must have a final Stock field that is initialized in the constructor (i.e., an instance field). Immediately afterwards, an explicit note in the problem statement (the numbered notes) requires that the stock attribute must be static (shared across all instances) and that acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice must be static. The provided solution implements stock as a static field (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()) and the template code constructs SealSaloon with a no-argument constructor, which aligns with the static interpretation. This inconsistency (instance final field initialized in the constructor vs. static shared field) in the problem statement will confuse students about whether to declare stock as an instance final field or as a static shared field and which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent. Preferred fix (aligns with template and solution): update the UML and the earlier textual description to state that SealSaloon.stock is a static (shared) field and keep the requirement that acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice are static. Alternatively, if the intended design is an instance final field, update the later note that mandates static methods/field and update the template/solution accordingly. Also reconcile the constructor requirement in the UML/text so it matches the chosen design (either document a no-arg constructor for a static shared stock, or require a constructor that initializes the instance final stock). Explicitly state in the problem statement which fields/methods must be static to avoid ambiguity.
